discoveries.choice: notes.txt holds the whole note as a single unstructured prose line rather than a structured or multi-line format
discoveries.whyItMatters: The plan's goal for a notes file is that its content is readable and complete; choosing single-line prose means any consumer (human or tool) must do string-level parsing rather than line- or section-level parsing, which constrains later additions such as multiple notes, tags, or metadata.

alternatives.option: Use a multi-line or keyed structure (e.g., one note per line, or heading/body sections)
alternatives.consequence: Would make the file extensible and machine-parseable, but adds format decisions and conventions beyond the minimal stated content.

alternatives.option: Keep one line but make it a structured single record (e.g., timestamp + text)
alternatives.consequence: Gains a bit of metadata for ordering, at the cost of extra syntax that the current content does not require.

recommendation.choice: Keep the single unstructured prose line
recommendation.reason: With only one note, structure would be speculative; the plain line satisfies the readability goal and can be restructured later when a second note or metadata actually appears.

discoveries.choice: The note text is lowercase, unpunctuated, and carries no heading, title, or terminating period
discoveries.whyItMatters: Presentation conventions affect how the note reads and whether later tooling can rely on consistent conventions; picking an intentionally informal, minimal style means the file's tone and grammar are unowned by the plan and left to the author's discretion.

alternatives.option: Use sentence case with terminal punctuation (e.g., "One line of notes.")
alternatives.consequence: Produces more conventionally polished prose, but imposes editorial rules the plan never asked for and would make the file inconsistent with casual shorthand notes.

alternatives.option: Add a title or header line above the note
alternatives.consequence: Improves discoverability in a long file, but is redundant for a one-line file and would add a second line that duplicates the same information.

recommendation.choice: Leave the note as lowercase, unpunctuated plain text with no heading
recommendation.reason: For a single-line note the wording is a cosmetic detail with no effect on the content's meaning, so it is best left to author discretion rather than fixed by contract.
